context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud, providing sub-50ms decisions and case management for analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, 7-year tamper-evident auditability, and zero-downtime model updates within a 25k EUR monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
*   **Payment Gateway / Shoppers:** External systems and end-users sending transaction authorizations.
*   **Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers:** Human actors reviewing suspicious payments and managing rules.
*   **API Gateway & Ingestion Layer:** Handles incoming traffic using TLS 1.3 and mTLS.
*   **Scoring Service:** Evaluates transactions against fraud rules and ML models.
*   **Case Management UI:** Interface for analysts to review flagged transactions without raw PAN access.
*   **Audit & Storage Layer:** Amazon S3 Object Lock with WORM compliance for 7-year retention.

## Relationships
*   **Payment Gateway to API Gateway:** Sends authorization requests via REST API over TLS 1.3.
*   **Scoring Service to Amazon DynamoDB:** Retrieves lookup data and records decision metadata via AWS SDK.
*   **Fraud Analysts to Case Management UI:** Accesses case queues via HTTPS with strict RBAC enforcement.
*   **Scoring Service to S3 Object Lock:** Writes tamper-evident audit logs using AWS KMS encryption.

## Technology Stack
*   **AWS ECS Fargate / AWS Lambda:** Chosen for serverless container orchestration to maintain a lean infrastructure footprint and fit the 3-engineer team capacity.
*   **Amazon DynamoDB:** Provides low-latency key-value data access to meet the P99 < 50ms latency requirement.
*   **Amazon S3 Object Lock & Glacier:** Enforces 7-year WORM compliance while optimizing storage costs to stay within the 25k EUR budget.
*   **AWS SageMaker Serverless:** Runs pre-trained ML models without managing distributed training clusters.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to deliver high throughput and sub-50ms latency while keeping operational overhead low enough for a three-engineer team. Strict data minimization and WORM storage ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability within the fixed budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time card-not-present payment fraud screening and case management for a mid-size payment processor in AWS (eu-west-1). It screens 3,000 authorizations per second, routes suspicious payments to analysts, and enforces strict PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
*   **Users:** Fraud Analysts, Risk Managers, Compliance Officers, Shoppers/End-Consumers
*   **External Systems:** Payment Gateway / Shoppers
*   **Containers:** Real-Time Scoring Engine, Case Management Service, Tokenization Proxy, Audit & Cryptographic Signer Sidecar, Model Management Service
*   **Data Stores & Infrastructure:** Amazon ECS with Fargate, Amazon ECR, Amazon S3 (WORM with Glacier), AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS CloudHSM

## Relationships
*   Payment Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Engine via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
*   Real-Time Scoring Engine to Tokenization Proxy via gRPC
*   Scoring Engine to Audit Sidecar via IPC / Local gRPC
*   Fraud Analysts to Case Management Service via HTTPS (OIDC/OAuth2 via AWS Cognito)
*   Audit Sidecar to S3 WORM Bucket via AWS SDK (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
*   **Compute:** AWS ECS with Fargate and Fargate Spot, using ECS Service Connect for mTLS to minimize operational overhead for a 3-person team.
*   **Security & Encryption:** AWS KMS (Customer-Managed Keys) and AWS CloudHSM for tamper-evident cryptographic signing and data-at-rest encryption.
*   **Secret & Token Management:** AWS Secrets Manager for secret zero and dedicated tokenization proxies for PCI-DSS scope reduction.
*   **Storage:** Amazon S3 with Object Lock (WORM) and Glacier Lifecycle Policies for 7-year immutable audit retention.

## Rationale
AWS ECS Fargate and managed services eliminate infrastructure management overhead, allowing a 3-person team to operate within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Memory-cached models and localized tokenization guarantee P99 latencies below 50 ms while satisfying strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and tamper-evident audit requirements.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under 50 milliseconds while providing case management for fraud analysts. It operates within AWS eu-west-1, ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Shoppers (External System)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate, ECS Service Connect)
- Tokenization Proxy (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Audit & Cryptographic Signer Sidecar (AWS ECS Fargate, AWS CloudHSM, AWS KMS)
- Case Management Service (AWS ECS Fargate, AWS Cognito)
- Model Management Service (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers (Users)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Shoppers -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Sends payment authorizations for fraud screening [HTTPS/TLS 1.3, mTLS, signed JWT]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Tokenization Proxy: Tokenizes payment data [gRPC over mTLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Audit & Cryptographic Signer Sidecar: Sends audit logs and attribution bitmasks for tamper-evident signing [Local IPC / Unix domain sockets]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen for operational simplicity with a 3-engineer team.
- AWS ECS Service Connect: Internal service mesh enforcing mTLS and zero-trust transport security.
- AWS CloudHSM & KMS: Cryptographic signing and secrets management for 7-year auditability and runtime decryption.
- AWS Application Auto Scaling (RequestCountPerTarget): Cost-optimized scaling staying within the 25,000 EUR/month budget.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless containers and managed AWS security services to achieve sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS within a strict 25,000 EUR budget. It minimizes PCI-DSS scope via tokenization proxies and ensures auditability via cryptographic sidecars managed by a three-engineer team.

Case Management Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Service provides a secure web interface for fraud analysts to review suspicious payment authorizations, manage queues, and inspect audit trails. It integrates strict compliance controls and high-performance components to meet PCI-DSS Level 1 mandates within a fixed infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers: End-users interacting with the system.
- Case Management Service: Core container hosted on AWS ECS Fargate.
- AWS Cognito: OIDC/OAuth2 identity provider managing user authentication and RBAC.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Tamper-evident 7-year audit storage using S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
- Amazon Redis: In-memory datastore for low-latency priority queue management.
- AWS X-Ray: Distributed tracing tool for observability.

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management Service: Reviews suspicious payments and manages queues via HTTPS (OIDC/OAuth2 via AWS Cognito).
- Case Management Service -> Amazon S3: Stores audit trails and case history via AWS SDK.
- Case Management Service -> Amazon Redis: Reads and writes priority queue states via TCP.

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration chosen for low operational overhead with a three-engineer team.
- AWS Cognito: Authentication provider ensuring PCI-DSS compliant session security and RBAC.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Compliant WORM storage ensuring 7-year tamper-evident auditability cost-effectively.
- Amazon Redis: Sorted sets used for high-performance priority queue management without database locks.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational burden for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS compliance. The selected tech stack ensures secure, low-latency case investigations and tamper-evident auditing within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint.

Tokenization Proxy.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present authorizations for a mid-size payment processor. Its core purpose is to screen transactions, route suspicious payments to analysts, and maintain PCI-DSS compliance under strict latency limits.]

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate, ECS Service Connect)
- Tokenization Proxy (AWS ECS Fargate)
- AWS KMS and AWS CloudHSM
- Payment Gateway / Shoppers
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Sends authorization requests [HTTPS/JSON]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Tokenization Proxy: Tokenizes sensitive payment data [gRPC with mTLS]
- Tokenization Proxy -> AWS KMS / CloudHSM: Performs format-preserving cryptographic tokenization [AWS SDK / TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Compute: AWS ECS Fargate for containerized microservices deployment within the 25,000 EUR budget
- Security: AWS KMS and AWS CloudHSM for stateless vaultless format-preserving encryption satisfying PCI-DSS Level 1
- Protocol: gRPC with mTLS via AWS Private CA for low-latency, secure internal communication
- Language: Go for the Tokenization Proxy to ensure high performance and minimal memory footprint

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and secure cryptographic isolation without violating the 50ms P99 latency requirement or the 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint. Stateless vaultless tokenization eliminates vulnerable database caches, protecting sensitive data while meeting high-throughput demands.]

Audit & Cryptographic Signer Sidecar.analysis:
## Overview
AWS-hosted real-time payment fraud screening system processing card-not-present authorizations with a tamper-evident 7-year audit sidecar. Designed for a 3-engineer team under a €25,000 monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Audit & Cryptographic Sidecar (AWS ECS Fargate, local encrypted tmpfs/EBS buffer)
- AWS KMS (Asymmetric signing and envelope encryption)
- Amazon S3 WORM Bucket with S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Object Lock

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Audit Sidecar: Sends logs [Local gRPC over mTLS]
- Audit Sidecar -> AWS KMS: Generates cryptographic signatures and seals log batches [AWS SDK (HTTPS)]
- Audit Sidecar -> Amazon S3 WORM Bucket: Stores immutable audit logs [AWS SDK (HTTPS)]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration within the €25,000 budget
- AWS KMS: Fully managed cryptographic signing replacing AWS CloudHSM to reduce operational toil
- Amazon S3 Object Lock & Glacier Flexible Retrieval: Cost-effective 7-year immutable retention
- Local encrypted tmpfs/EBS: Secure buffering for the 1-minute failover window (R-07)

## Rationale
AWS KMS and S3 WORM eliminate operational overhead while enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability. Encrypted local buffering protects P99 latency SLAs under 50 ms at 3,000 TPS.

Model Management Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Model Management Service enables zero-downtime updates and governance for fraud scoring models. It provides risk managers with self-service model promotion, explainability previews, and performance dashboards while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts and Risk Managers (Users)
- Model Management Service (AWS ECS Fargate Container)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (ECS Fargate Container)
- Audit & Cryptographic Signer Sidecar (AWS ECS Fargate Container)
- AWS S3 & AWS KMS (Storage and Encryption)
- AWS Cognito (Identity Provider)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts to Model Management Service via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 (OAuth2/OIDC via AWS Cognito)
- Model Management Service to AWS S3 via HTTPS (Model artifact storage and version manifests)
- Model Management Service to Audit & Cryptographic Signer via gRPC/Internal Network (Model promotion and rollback audit logs)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine to AWS S3 via HTTPS (Model hot-reloading and signature verification)

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration aligned with the 3-engineer team constraint and €25k/month budget.
- AWS S3 with Object Lock: Storage for model artifacts and 7-year audit retention compliance.
- AWS KMS: Customer-managed encryption keys for at-rest model security.
- AWS Cognito: OIDC/OAuth2 authentication and RBAC for risk managers.
- AWS CloudWatch: Metrics and performance dashboard integration.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures zero-downtime model updates and strict 7-year auditability while respecting operational limits. Leveraging managed AWS services minimizes maintenance overhead for the three-engineer team.
